response.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT ID, COUNT(*) AS n FROM Examination GROUP BY ID), f AS (SELECT ID, n, n * 1.0 / SUM(n) OVER () AS frac FROM g), a AS (SELECT ID, n, frac, AVG(frac) OVER () AS avg_frac FROM f) SELECT ID, n AS num_examinations, frac AS fraction, frac - avg_frac AS excess_over_average FROM a WHERE frac > avg_frac ORDER BY excess_over_average DESC LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: Examinations with NULL ID form a single group, which GROUP BY does naturally. That group is included when computing the total and the average fraction. The average is taken over all groups, so it equals 1 divided by the number of groups.
Ties at the 10th position are broken arbitrarily, because the request gives no tie-breaker.
